PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Self-control is part of the fruit of the Holy Spirit. In this sub-strand you will read Galatians 5:23-25, practise decisions that the Holy Spirit would approve, and learn to avoid sex, ungodly films, and drug use, which defile the body.

## Strand 5.0: The Church
Sub-strand 5.6: Self-control
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23-25
b) make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit
c) demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body
d) live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you practice self- control?

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is portrayed as learners list choices they make in their day-to-day lives.
• Imagination and creativity: the skill of originality is exhibited as learners role-play ‘making decisions that portray self- control.’

## Values
• Responsibility is inculcated as learners list and avoid things that can defile their bodies.
• Integrity: learners exhibit self-discipline by not engaging in acts that can defile them e.g. watching ungodly movies.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Human sexuality: learners list choices they make in their day-to-day lives concerning sexual purity.
• Child care and protection: learners are empowered to exercise self-control by not defiling their bodies.
• Alcohol and substance abuse: learners list things that can defile them e.g. drug use and abuse.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing and role play.
• English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 The Church, Sub-strand 5.6 Self-control
• Galatians 5:23-25

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Self-control and right decisions

LESSON 1: SELF-CONTROL AND RIGHT DECISIONS
==========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain self-control from Galatians 5:23-25.
• Choose decisions that show self-control and follow the Holy Spirit.

Curriculum outcomes: a) ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23-25; b) make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit

## Introduction
You often choose quickly: to answer back, to push, to copy, or to wait. Galatians 5:23-25 calls that power to choose well self-control, and it tells people who belong to Christ to walk by the Holy Spirit.

## Notes
### Galatians 5:23-25
Read the verses. They say that the fruit includes meekness and temperance, and that against such things there is no law. People who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.

Temperance is self-control. It means you stop yourself from doing wrong even when you feel like doing it. A learner shows it by waiting, by closing the mouth before an insult, and by refusing a dare.

"Crucified the flesh" is a Bible picture. It does not tell a child to harm his or her body. It means that sinful desires are not in charge any more. People who belong to Christ say no to those desires.

"Walk in the Spirit" means live each day in step with the Holy Spirit. If the Spirit gives us life, our choices should follow him.

### Choices in a day
In groups, list choices you really make:

- To fight, or to walk away
- To cheat in a test, or to do your own work
- To shout at a brother or sister, or to speak calmly
- To grab the biggest share, or to share fairly
- To watch whatever is playing, or to switch off what is ungodly
- To follow friends into a wrong plan, or to say no

A right decision is one that fits the Holy Spirit's fruit: love, peace, goodness and self-control. Before you choose, you can pray, "Holy Spirit, help me to choose what pleases God."

### Role-play
Acting the choice helps the body remember it. One learner presses you to cheat. You refuse and do your own work. One learner insults you. You do not hit back. You report the insult if it continues. The point of the play is the controlled decision, not the laugh.

## Key words
• self-control — stopping yourself from doing wrong; temperance in Galatians 5:23
• walk in the Spirit — live each day in step with the Holy Spirit
• decision — a choice you make and then act on

## Worked examples

### Example 1
During a test, a friend whispers, "Let me see your answers." What decision shows self-control guided by the Holy Spirit?

Working:
1. Galatians 5:23 names self-control as part of the fruit.
2. Cheating is not goodness or faithfulness.
3. Walking in the Spirit means choosing what pleases God even when a friend asks.

Answer: Say no, cover your work, and do your own test.

## Activity: Role-play decisions that show self-control
You will need: Bible
1. Read Galatians 5:23-25.
2. In groups, list choices you make in day-to-day life.
3. Role-play making decisions that portray self-control, for example refusing to cheat or refusing to fight.
4. After each play, say which choice followed the Holy Spirit.

## Practice
1. What word in Galatians 5:23 means self-control?
2. What does "walk in the Spirit" mean?
3. Does "crucified the flesh" tell a child to harm the body?
4. Give two right decisions a learner can make at school.

## Summary
• Self-control is temperance, part of the fruit of the Holy Spirit.
• People who belong to Christ do not let sinful desires rule them.
• Right decisions follow the Holy Spirit in ordinary daily choices.

### Answers to practice
1. Temperance.
2. To live each day in step with the Holy Spirit, so that your choices follow him.
3. No. It is a picture meaning that sinful desires are not in charge of a person who belongs to Christ.
4. Any two: do your own work, walk away from a fight, speak calmly, share fairly, or say no to a wrong plan.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Keeping the body from what defiles it

LESSON 2: KEEPING THE BODY FROM WHAT DEFILES IT
===============================================

## What you will learn
• List things that defile the body and say how to avoid them.
• Describe a godly life guided by the Holy Spirit.

Curriculum outcomes: c) demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body; d) live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit

## Introduction
Self-control protects the body. Some choices do not only break a rule. They defile the body, which means they make it unclean before God. Galatians 5:25 tells believers who live by the Spirit to walk by the Spirit.

## Notes
### Things that defile
To defile means to make dirty or unfit for God. In this lesson, name these:

- Engaging in sex. Children are not to take part in sexual acts. That includes someone touching you in a sexual way or asking you to touch them. Say no and tell a trusted adult.
- Watching ungodly movies. Films and videos that show sexual sin, cruelty or evil as something to copy make the eyes and the mind unclean.
- Drug use and abuse. Alcohol, cigarettes, miraa and other drugs harm the body and take away self-control.

These are the examples to remember. Each one is a choice. Self-control is the choice to refuse them.

### How to avoid defiling the body
- Do not go to a hidden place with a person who wants sexual acts. Leave and tell a parent, guardian or teacher, even if you were told to keep it secret.
- Switch off an ungodly movie. Do not pass the phone to a friend so they can watch it too.
- Do not taste alcohol or other drugs to "try". The first try is already the wrong decision.
- Choose friends who will not push you into these things.
- Keep busy with work, games and church.
- Pray and ask the Holy Spirit for strength to say no.
- Remember that your body is to honour God.

### A godly life
A godly life is a life guided by the Holy Spirit. It matches Galatians 5:25: if we live in the Spirit, we also walk in the Spirit. That life is honest, kind, and clean. Integrity means you refuse the film or the drug even when the adult has left the room.

You are cared for and protected when you exercise this self-control. Parents, teachers and the church stand with a child who reports danger. Living in a godly way is not a lonely fight. It is walking with the Holy Spirit and with people who love you.

## Key words
• defile — to make the body or life unclean before God
• ungodly — against God's way; a film or act that leads away from him
• godly — following God's way, guided by the Holy Spirit
• drug abuse — using drugs, including alcohol and cigarettes, in a way that harms the body

## Activity: A song on self-control
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Galatians 5:23-25 again.
2. List things that can defile you, including engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, and drug use and abuse.
3. Say how you can avoid defiling your body.
4. Compose a song on self-control from Galatians 5:23-25 and sing it.

## Practice
1. Name three things that can defile a person.
2. What should a child do if someone asks them to take part in a sexual act and to keep it secret?
3. Why is "just trying" alcohol or another drug a failure of self-control?
4. What is a godly life according to Galatians 5:25?

## Summary
• Sex, ungodly movies, and drug use defile the body.
• Self-control says no, switches off the film, and refuses drugs.
• A godly life walks in the Holy Spirit even when nobody is watching.

### Answers to practice
1. Engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, and drug use and abuse.
2. Say no, leave, and tell a parent, guardian or teacher.
3. Drug use defiles and harms the body. The first try is already the wrong decision.
4. A life that walks in the Spirit, guided by the Holy Spirit, because we live by the Spirit.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.6 SELF-CONTROL
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Self-control in Galatians 5:23 is called:
   A. Temperance
   B. A den of thieves
   C. A tax
   D. A hymn

2. "Walk in the Spirit" means:
   A. Live in step with the Holy Spirit
   B. Walk to the market only
   C. Ignore every choice
   D. Follow every friend

3. A friend wants you to cheat. The decision guided by the Holy Spirit is to:
   A. Show the answers quickly
   B. Do your own work and say no
   C. Tear the friend's paper
   D. Hide both papers

4. Which choice shows self-control in a quarrel?
   A. Hitting first
   B. Walking away and speaking calmly
   C. Gathering a crowd to fight
   D. Breaking a desk

5. Which of these defiles the body?
   A. Doing homework
   B. Drug use and abuse
   C. Closing a tap
   D. Reciting a Bible verse

6. Watching ungodly movies is dangerous because:
   A. They can make the mind unclean and teach sin
   B. They are always about science
   C. The Bible tells children to copy them
   D. They replace food

7. If someone asks a child to engage in sex and keep it secret, the child should:
   A. Agree and keep quiet
   B. Say no, leave, and tell a trusted adult
   C. Ask friends to come and watch
   D. Wait for a year and then tell

8. Why should you not try alcohol or other drugs?

9. A godly life guided by the Holy Spirit means:
   A. Doing right only when a teacher is watching
   B. Walking in the Spirit in daily choices, including secret ones
   C. Never praying
   D. Joining every group

10. Give one way to avoid defiling your body this week.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.6 SELF-CONTROL
========================================

1. A. Temperance
   Temperance means self-control.

2. A. Live in step with the Holy Spirit
   Galatians 5:25 says if we live in the Spirit, we should also walk in the Spirit.

3. B. Do your own work and say no
   Self-control chooses the honest action.

4. B. Walking away and speaking calmly
   Self-control stops the blow and chooses peace.

5. B. Drug use and abuse
   Drug use and abuse is one of the things the lesson names as defiling.

6. A. They can make the mind unclean and teach sin
   Ungodly films are listed among things that defile.

7. B. Say no, leave, and tell a trusted adult
   Self-control includes refusing sexual acts and reporting them.

8. They harm the body, take away self-control, and defile a person. The try itself is the wrong choice.
   Drug use and abuse are to be avoided, not sampled.

9. B. Walking in the Spirit in daily choices, including secret ones
   Galatians 5:25 calls believers to walk in the Spirit.

10. Any one: refuse sexual acts and report them, switch off ungodly movies, refuse drugs, choose good friends, or pray for self-control.
   Avoiding what defiles is how self-control protects the body.
